channel.title: JustinCredible EV
channel.description: Electric vehicles, charging, batteries and self-driving tech.

item.title: Tesla Invites Select Buyers to Order a Cybercab for Personal Use at $29,990 Plus a Required $299 Monthly Subscription
item.description: Tesla began inviting select customers on November 13, 2026, to order a Cybercab for personal use. It costs $29,990 before taxes, requires a $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription to operate, and only works inside Tesla's Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida.

item.title: Tesla Drops the $41,990 Model Y AWD; the Cheapest All-Wheel-Drive Model Y Is Now $49,990
item.description: Tesla removed the base Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its U.S. online configurator on November 13, 2026, about nine months after launch. The least expensive AWD Model Y you can order is now the $49,990 Premium AWD.

item.title: Tesla Winding Down Cybertruck Production at Gigafactory Texas Around Mid-2027
item.description: Elon Musk said Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercab robotaxis, after U.S. sales missed early targets.

item.title: Tesla and SpaceX Are Officially Exploring a Merger, but Nothing's Agreed Yet
item.description: Both companies' boards have formed special committees of independent directors to study a possible combination. Musk is recused, no terms exist, and Tesla would need a yes from half of all its shares.

item.title: Mercedes-AMG's First In-House SUV Is Electric and Tops Out at 1,153 hp
item.description: The new Mercedes-AMG GT SUV is the first full-size SUV AMG developed entirely in-house in its 59-year history. The top GT 63 has three electric motors, 1,153 hp in U.S. trim, up to 710 kW charging and a simulated V8 soundtrack.

item.title: BYD's New Seagull EV Starts at $9,800 in China, With 5-Minute Charging on Pricier Trims
item.description: BYD launched the second-generation Seagull in China on October 20 from 65,900 yuan (about $9,800). It's bigger, seats five and is rear-wheel drive, and its three bigger-battery trims add Flash Charging that goes from 10% to 70% in five minutes.

item.title: Tesla's Cybercab Expands Beyond Austin, and Dallas Is Next
item.description: On its Q3 earnings call, Tesla said its two-seat Cybercab robotaxi expands to Dallas next month, with more cities and fleet sales by the end of 2026. NHTSA is still reviewing whether a car with no brake pedal or mirrors meets federal rules.

item.title: Tesla’s New FSD Trick: A Panic Button That Presses Itself
item.description: FSD Supervised v14.3.9 is rolling out with Automatic Collision Evasion on HW4—FSD can jump in while you’re driving manually if a crash looks imminent or you’re not attentive. Here’s the lighthearted consumer take.

item.title: FSD v14 Just Got ACE — Ashok Says v15 Is the Real Leap
item.description: Hours after FSD v14.3.9’s Automatic Collision Evasion rollout chatter, Tesla AI lead Ashok Elluswamy previewed v15: earlier hazard prediction, faster reactions, and better collision avoidance. Here’s the light, hopeful consumer take.

item.title: Tesla Just Said ‘Go for Launch’ — Roadster Reveal Locked for October 1
item.description: Tesla posted “Go for launch” with a 10.01 graphic and a countdown on the Roadster page. After years of delays since the Nov 2017 debut, the next-gen sports car finally has a reveal date — thruster lore included. Here’s the evening poll.

item.title: Cybertruck + Powerwall 3: Tesla Just Made Multi-Day Home Backup a Team Sport
item.description: Tesla’s Cybertruck Powershare can now back up a home together with Powerwall 3—extending outage runtime by more than three days. Here’s what changed and why it matters.
